title: Singular partitive of common -is words
summary: For these -is words, keep the base consonants and add -ta/-tä: kaunis (“beautiful”) → kaunista.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

These selected -is words add -ta/-tä to the unchanged dictionary form in singular partitive. Vowel harmony selects the ending. Keep one t in raitista. Other -is words belong to different plural families, so learn this selected group with its words.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Keep kaunis and add -ta: kaunis → kaunista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “beautiful”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep kallis and add -ta: kallis → kallista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “expensive”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep valmis and add -ta: valmis → valmista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “ready”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep one t and add -ta: raitis → raitista.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “sober”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep tiivis and add -tä: tiivis → tiivistä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “compact”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not copy the double-i plural stem into the singular.
Keep the base consonants in raitista.
